title: Sectionwise quasi-isomorphisms induce quasi-isomorphisms of finite ordered Cech totals
statement: Let V:Fin r → Opens(X) be any finite open family on a scheme X, and let i:F → J be a map of cochain complexes of O_X-module sheaves. Suppose sections over every increasing-tuple intersection send i to a quasi-isomorphism of complexes over its section ring. Then the map on the ordered Cech totals [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex] is a quasi-isomorphism. No cover condition, boundedness or flasqueness is assumed. The category of module sheaves is [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: Restrict the section complexes over each intersection to the global section ring. Restriction of scalars preserves homology and the stipulated quasi-isomorphisms.

In each nonnegative Cech degree identify the vertical column with the finite product of the section complexes. Reuse alternatingCechColumnProjection and alternatingCechColumnProjection_isIso from Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.QCohAlternatingCechResolutionQuasiIso instead of defining or proving them again. Module products commute with homology, and naturality of these projections makes the column map a quasi-isomorphism.

Reuse alternatingCechDouble_strictlyGE and alternatingCechDouble_strictlyLE from Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.QCohAlternatingCechResolutionQuasiIso: columns outside 0,...,r-1 are zero. Apply the integer finite-column total-comparison theorem. Only the support and projection helpers are used; the quasi-coherent-resolution theorem is not used.
